I will plant a winter wheat and summer maize rotation on the same land. In Quzhou County, that is the most steady way for me to use the full year, match the local climate, and reduce my market and weather risk. I am 55, so I would not choose a crop that needs too much fine hand labor or has unstable sales. I would keep the plan simple and familiar, use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, and rely on the practices I know can be managed with ordinary machinery and irrigation. I will do a plough before wheat to loosen the soil and help the base fertilizer go down, then use rotary tillage before summer maize because the time after wheat harvest is tight. I will put most fertilizer on as base plus a topdressing at key growth stages, irrigate several times for wheat because spring moisture is often not enough, and irrigate maize fewer times because the summer rainy season helps. I will control weeds, aphids, rust, and other common problems when needed, but I will not spray more than necessary because cost matters. I will assume I am managing 20 mu of normal irrigated farmland, and I will use the same 20 mu in rotation across the year.
